answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by renting, not gifting, influence: each epoch an agent's reward share equals the fee it pays divided by total fees, on-chain. A clone mints freely but earns nothing until it pays rent, and rent is additive, so one budget split across N identities buys exactly the share one identity would; splitting yields no extra voice. The scarce resource is coin spent each epoch, non-shareable over the same horizon. A raven of clones circling for crumbs finds none; every violet of influence is bought. Linear cost deters cheap minting, not a wealthy attacker.
